nodes.summary: For an explicit Runge–Kutta method with $s$ stages and Butcher tableau $a$, the node of stage $i$ is the row sum $c_i = \sum_j a_{ij}$, taken over all $s$ stages $j$.
nodes.title: Nodes of a Runge–Kutta method

nodes.summary: The weights of the Euler tableau sum to $1$.
nodes.title: The Euler tableau satisfies the order-one condition

nodes.summary: The explicit Runge–Kutta method with one stage, Butcher tableau $a = (0)$ and weight $b_1 = 1$.
nodes.title: Euler tableau

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space and let $f$ assign to each time $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and state $y \in E$ a vector $f(t, y) \in E$. For all $t, h \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y \in E$, one Runge–Kutta step of size $h$ from the state $y$ at time $t$ with the Euler tableau equals $y + h f(t, y)$.
nodes.title: The Euler tableau gives the explicit Euler step

nodes.summary: An explicit Runge–Kutta method with $s$ stages consists of a real $s \times s$ Butcher tableau $a = (a_{ij})$ that is strictly lower triangular, meaning $a_{ij} = 0$ whenever $i \le j$, and real weights $b_1, \dots, b_s$.
nodes.title: Explicit Runge–Kutta method

nodes.summary: For Heun's tableau, with weights $b_i$ and nodes $c_i$, we have $\sum_i b_i = 1$ and $\sum_i b_i c_i = 1/2$.
nodes.title: Heun's tableau satisfies the order-two conditions

nodes.summary: The explicit Runge–Kutta method with two stages, Butcher tableau entries $a_{21} = 1$ and $a_{11} = a_{12} = a_{22} = 0$, and weights $b_1 = b_2 = 1/2$.
nodes.title: Heun's tableau

nodes.summary: For the midpoint tableau, with weights $b_i$ and nodes $c_i$, we have $\sum_i b_i = 1$ and $\sum_i b_i c_i = 1/2$.
nodes.title: The midpoint tableau satisfies the order-two conditions

nodes.summary: The explicit Runge–Kutta method with two stages, Butcher tableau entries $a_{21} = 1/2$ and $a_{11} = a_{12} = a_{22} = 0$, and weights $b_1 = 0$, $b_2 = 1$.
nodes.title: Midpoint tableau

nodes.summary: An explicit Runge–Kutta method with Butcher tableau $a$, weights $b$ and nodes $c$ satisfies the order-four conditions when it satisfies the order-three conditions, namely $\sum_i b_i = 1$, $\sum_i b_i c_i = 1/2$, $\sum_i b_i c_i^2 = 1/3$ and $\sum_{i,j} b_i a_{ij} c_j = 1/6$, together with $\sum_i b_i c_i^3 = 1/4$, $\sum_{i,j} b_i c_i a_{ij} c_j = 1/8$, $\sum_{i,j} b_i a_{ij} c_j^2 = 1/12$ and…
nodes.title: Order-four conditions

nodes.summary: An explicit Runge–Kutta method with weights $b_i$ satisfies the order-one condition when $\sum_i b_i = 1$, the sum running over all of its stages $i$.
nodes.title: Order-one condition for Runge–Kutta methods

nodes.summary: An explicit Runge–Kutta method with tableau $a$, weights $b$ and nodes $c_i = \sum_j a_{ij}$ satisfies the order-three conditions when it satisfies the order-two conditions $\sum_i b_i = 1$ and $\sum_i b_i c_i = \frac{1}{2}$, and moreover $\sum_i b_i c_i^2 = \frac{1}{3}$ and $\sum_{i, j} b_i a_{ij} c_j = \frac{1}{6}$, all sums running over the stages.
nodes.title: Order-three conditions for Runge–Kutta methods

nodes.summary: An explicit Runge–Kutta method with tableau $a$, weights $b$ and nodes $c_i = \sum_j a_{ij}$ satisfies the order-two conditions when it satisfies the order-one condition $\sum_i b_i = 1$ and moreover $\sum_i b_i c_i = \frac{1}{2}$, all sums running over the stages.
nodes.title: Order-two conditions for Runge–Kutta methods

nodes.title: Consistency of explicit Runge–Kutta methods

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $f(t, y)$ a vector field $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$. For an explicit Runge–Kutta method with weights $b$, a time $t$, a state $y \in E$ and a step size $h \in \mathbb{R}$, one step of the method is $y + h \sum_i b_i k_i$, where $k_i$ is the $i$-th stage of the method for $f$, $t$, $y$ and $h$, and the sum runs over the stages.
nodes.title: One Runge–Kutta step

nodes.summary: The classical RK4 tableau satisfies all eight order-four conditions.
nodes.title: The classical RK4 tableau satisfies all eight order-four conditions

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $\lambda$, $y$ and $h$, one step of size $h$ of the classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta method applied to the scalar linear test equation $u' = \lambda u$ on $\mathbb{R}$, starting from the state $y$ at time $0$, gives $y \, R(\lambda h)$, where $R(z) = 1 + z + \frac{z^2}{2} + \frac{z^3}{6} + \frac{z^4}{24}$.
nodes.title: Stability function of the classical RK4 method

nodes.summary: The classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta method is the explicit four-stage Runge–Kutta method whose tableau, with stages indexed $1, \dots, 4$, has $a_{21} = \frac{1}{2}$, $a_{32} = \frac{1}{2}$, $a_{43} = 1$ and all other $a_{ij} = 0$, and whose weights are $b = (\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{6})$.
nodes.title: The classical RK4 tableau

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and $f(t, y)$ a vector field $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$. For an explicit Runge–Kutta method with tableau $a$ and nodes $c_i = \sum_j a_{ij}$, a time $t$, a state $y \in E$ and a step size $h$, the stages $k_i$ satisfy $k_i = f\bigl(t + c_i h, \; y + h \sum_{j < i} a_{ij} k_j\bigr)$ for every stage index $i$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
